title: The MInimizing RIsk of CLotting Events Trial
official: Optimizing the Implementation of Personalized Risk-prediction Models for Venous Thromboembolism Among Hospitalized Adults: The MInimizing RIsk of CLotting Events (MIRICLE) Trial
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate whether the implementation of a real-time prognostic model can effectively identify and prevent blood clots among hospitalized patients. The main questions it aims to answer is:

1. Can the prognostic model reduce rates of hospital-acquired blood clots (also known as hospital-acquired venous thromboembolisms)?
2. Is the prognostic model an effective tool for initiating timely and appropriate preventive treatment (i.e., thromboprophylaxis)?

Researchers will compare the intervention arm with the control arm (standard of care) to determine whether the intervention reduces rates of blood clots and improves initiation of preventive treatment.

The intervention (clinical decision support that displays the prognostic model's output) will be implemented by displaying a risk score in clinicians' workflow in the electronic health record (EHR) to notify clinicians of patients who are at higher risk for sustaining a blood clot. The intervention will not dictate patient care and clinicians will continue to use their clinical knowledge and judgment in their clinical decision-making.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* 18 years of age
* Admitted to an inpatient setting at Vanderbilt Adult Hospital within study period

Exclusion Criteria:

* Under the age of 18.
sponsor: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)
